hook: M G U, B Com Honours, Semester Six. Cost Accounting.
Tender or Quotations. Question fourteen, from Doctor Jayan's Cost Accounting Methods, pages two ninety-two to two ninety-three.
A company has to quote a price for a new machine, and it wants a profit of twenty percent on the selling price.
What price should it quote? Let's solve it in three simple steps.
question: Here is the question. The accounts of National Limited showed the following.
Direct materials, seven lakh rupees.
Direct wages, five lakh forty thousand.
Works overhead, one lakh sixty-two thousand.
And establishment overhead, one lakh twelve thousand.
What price should the company quote to manufacture a machine which will require an expenditure of one thousand rupees in material, and eight hundred rupees in wages,
so that it will yield a profit of twenty percent on selling price?
Notice: the profit is on the selling price, not on cost. Keep that in mind.
step1: Step one. Prepare the cost sheet of National Limited.
Direct materials, seven lakh. Add direct wages, five lakh forty thousand.
That gives the Prime Cost: twelve lakh forty thousand rupees.
Add works overhead, one lakh sixty-two thousand.
That gives the Works Cost: fourteen lakh two thousand rupees.
Add establishment overhead, one lakh twelve thousand.
That gives the Cost of Production: fifteen lakh fourteen thousand rupees.
Now we use these figures to find the overhead rates.
step2: Step two. Find the overhead rates, and the rate of profit.
One. Works overhead rate, on direct wages.
Works overhead into hundred, over direct wages.
One lakh sixty-two thousand into hundred, over five lakh forty thousand. That is thirty percent.
Two. Establishment overhead rate, on works cost.
Establishment overhead into hundred, over works cost.
One lakh twelve thousand into hundred, over fourteen lakh two thousand. That is seven point nine eight eight six percent.
Rounded off, we take eight percent.
The profit is twenty percent on sales. We convert it to a rate on cost.
Profit on cost equals twenty, over hundred minus twenty, into hundred.
That is twenty over eighty, into hundred. Twenty-five percent on cost.
Why? If the selling price is hundred, the profit is twenty, so the cost is eighty. And twenty on eighty is twenty-five percent.
One more point. When the question does not give the bases, works overhead is absorbed as a percentage of direct wages, and establishment overhead as a percentage of works cost.
step3: Step three. The statement showing the quotation price of the machine.
Direct material, one thousand. Add direct wages, eight hundred.
Prime cost, one thousand eight hundred rupees.
Add works overhead, thirty percent of wages. Eight hundred into thirty, over hundred, is two hundred and forty.
Works cost, two thousand and forty rupees.
Add establishment overhead, eight percent of works cost. Two thousand and forty into eight, over hundred, is one hundred and sixty-three rupees, twenty paise.
Cost of production, the total cost, two thousand two hundred and three rupees, twenty paise.
Add profit. Twenty percent on sales is twenty over eighty on cost.
Two thousand two hundred and three rupees twenty paise, into twenty, over eighty, is five hundred and fifty rupees, eighty paise.
So the quotation price is two thousand seven hundred and fifty-four rupees.
traps: Now, three traps students fall into in the exam.
Trap one. Taking twenty percent of the cost as profit. That gives two thousand six hundred and forty-three rupees, eighty-four paise. Wrong!
The profit is on the selling price, so use twenty over eighty on cost.
Quick check: five hundred and fifty rupees eighty paise is exactly twenty percent of two thousand seven hundred and fifty-four.
Trap two. The wrong base. Works overhead goes on direct wages. Establishment overhead goes on works cost, not on wages or prime cost.
Trap three. Writing eight percent with no working. Show the formula, and write rounded off, when seven point nine eight eight six becomes eight.
recap: Step two, the rates: thirty percent, eight percent, and twenty-five percent on cost.
Step three, the quotation: two thousand seven hundred and fifty-four rupees.
